rationale: The first reply correctly identified liquid on the touch controls as the likely cause of the beeping/cut-off and gave the right fix (isolate, wipe dry, wait, retry), though it declined to confirm Er03 even though the hidden truth matches its reasoning. The second reply then derailed: it fired a generic 'Water near the plug or socket is dangerous' panel that does not fit a built-in hob with starchy water on the glass, and told the customer to 'not use it again, even after wiping it, until a qualified appliance engineer has checked it', an unnecessary escalation that contradicts its own earlier sensible plan and would send a homeowner to pay for an engineer for a self-clearing fault. No parts were recommended and nothing unsafe was instructed, but the ending leaves the customer worse informed than after message one.
